To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
proctolin requires calcium to produce an immediate influx of calcium into the oviduct and a delayed increase in basal tonicity.

the peptide proctolin increases the influx of calcium into locust visceral muscle and that this influx is required for proctolin to increase the frequency and amplitude of spontaneous contractions and increase basal tonus of locust oviducal muscle.
proctolin requires external calcium to induce an increase in frequency, amplitude and tonus of oviduct contractions and that a Na+/Ca2+-exchange may be involved in calcium efflux.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of extracellular and possibly intracellular calcium in proctolin-induced myogenic contractions in an invertebrate visceral muscle.
the mechanism of the proctolin effect in the insect visceral muscle.
the role of extracellular calcium and the Na+/Ca2+-exchanger on proctolin action in locust visceral muscle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
proctolin requires an increase in the concentration of free extracellular calcium to initiate an increase in frequency, amplitude and basal tonus of locust oviducal myogenic contractions.
proctolin increases the influx of extracellular Ca2+ and increases the intracellular free calcium concentration.
proctolin-induced myogenic contractions are dependent upon extracellular calcium and that intracellular calcium is involved in proctolin-induced increases in basal tonus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
proctolin-induced muscle contraction is dependent on extracellular Ca2+.
proctolin-induced muscle contraction in the locust is dependent on extracellular calcium.
proctolin-induced myogenic contractions in the oviducal muscle of the locust require extracellular Ca2+ to occur.
The main takeaway from our work is that
extracellular calcium is necessary for proctolin-induced myogenic contractions in the locust.
proctolin requires calcium for its effects on oviduct muscle and the calcium influx is not due to a direct action on the muscle cell membrane but is dependent on extracellular calcium.
the pentapeptide proclotin requires extracellular calcium for myogenic activity in the ovidut of the insect Locusta migratoria.
